# Synthetic reading notes / 虚构研究摘录

These are invented teaching materials, not published studies or real participant
data. DemoA and DemoB are demonstration identifiers, not references to cite.

## DemoA — Table 1
A made-up pilot compares reading sessions with and without a short break.
The sessions with a break have higher immediate recall scores.
No random assignment was used. Prior knowledge could explain the difference.

## DemoB — Table 2
A second made-up pilot also records a positive association between a short break
and immediate recall. It uses one reading task and a small convenience sample.
It does not measure recall after a week.

## Normalization decision
Both notes support a narrow association claim, CLM-1. They do not establish a
causal effect or lasting improvement. CLM-2 remains an evidence gap.

The supplied CSV and decision log demonstrate this reviewed normalization.
The CLI does not infer these judgments by reading arbitrary prose or PDFs.
